D.t: Lynne Walz trails by 3.6 and wins 24% of simulations. Closing it takes about 14,146 voters switching sides, or 28,293 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +10.2 and D +3.0. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is R +4.4. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Education Reform Now Advocacy (D) at D +0.3; your worst is New York Times/Siena at R +13.7. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Douglas, a projected net 65,038 votes; Lancaster, a projected net 32,662 votes; Sarpy, a projected net 6,415 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sarpy, D +8.3, 10.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lynne Walz runs furthest behind in Platte, Madison, Washington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 44 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.49 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 45 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.48 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 49 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.00 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Lynne Walz: Immigration voters 12 to 84, Small counties 28 to 67, Men 41 to 55. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$860K cash against $7.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 39% of the 222,007 ballots in Nebraska so far, against 44% for the other party. That is 4.3 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points toward Lynne Walz. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Cash: $7.5M in the bank against $860K for Lynne Walz.

R.t: Jim Pillen leads by 3.6 in the forecast and wins 76% of simulations. The cushion is about 28,293 votes; a one point swing is about 3,876 voters changing sides.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 52 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.49 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 51 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.48 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 47 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.00 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jim Pillen: Independents 24 to 68, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 30 to 65, Moderates 30 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
